input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete ("any product or service that competes with Vendor"), covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition, in any territory, for the term plus 24 months. That is walk-away territory on two counts: a post-term restraint longer than 12 months and undefined scope; it also fails every fallback element (no named product, post-term application, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out). It further contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." We therefore reverse the prohibition to the preferred position so Customer carries no non-compete or field-of-use restriction, leaving Section 12.3 consistent.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Remove the Customer non-compete in Section 12.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or services we may develop, buy or sell, so we have removed the prohibition in Section 12.4 and its 24-month post-term tail; this also resolves the conflict with Section 12.3, which confirms we gave no non-compete commitment. If the relationship genuinely needs protection, we could discuss a fallback limited to a single named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ops.newText: Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
